analysis.title: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. (BMY): Quarter As Expected, Pipeline Readouts Continue to Overshadow With LOEs Creeping Closer
key_insights: BMY closed +1.4% after generally inline 3Q26 results, lagging the DRG index (+3.4%). GS says the 3Q26 First Take was a modest beat and raise. Focus is on clinical readouts and on legacy-portfolio headwinds ahead of the patent cliffs (loss of exclusivity, LOE).

The milvexian secondary stroke prevention (SSP) readout is the key pipeline event before year-end. GS investor conversations show concern about risk/reward into the readout, given the high bar set by Bayer's asundexian and potential readacross to the Afib trial, which is the greatest swing factor on GS's DCF for BMY.

Management's milvexian framing was consistent with prior commentary: confidence in the SSP trial design, based on a Phase 2 trial showing 30% stroke risk reduction, with careful dose selection and a randomization window chosen for best efficacy. On Afib, management said the trial matters but should be seen in the context of a broader pipeline.

Growth portfolio: Opdivo Qvantig +5% vs consensus, with about 12% of the global Opdivo franchise converted to SubQ (vs 10%/7%/5%/3% in the prior 4 quarters) and US conversion about 16%. Breyanzi +8%, Sotyktu +16%, Yervoy +5% and Opdualag +4% also beat consensus.
Cobenfy missed consensus by about 16% on inventory destocking. Management said TRx grew 3% sequentially in 3Q26 and expects sales to follow volume growth more closely going forward.

2027 priorities: sustain growth portfolio momentum (8 growth products each annualizing above $1bn on 3Q26 sales), turn pipeline progress into filings, approvals and launches (CelMOD Zynbexis recently approved), and deliver $2bn of productivity efficiencies by end of 2027, which is on track.

Other pre-year-end catalysts: ADEPT program data for Cobenfy at CTAD (Nov 16-19) and the Phase 3 Sotyktu SLE study. A Sjogren's Phase 3 Sotyktu readout is due in 2027. GS sees these as more incremental than stock-moving.

Business development is a top capital allocation priority. Management is evaluating multiple deal structures (partnerships, licensing, acquisitions) and is agnostic on size. GS believes deals that add to near-term revenue growth, rather than early-stage assets, could be well received.

AI efforts: management cited a 20-30% reduction in drug testing timelines and halving the time from target selection to lead molecule identification. GS says this is a growing investor focus across Pharma.

GS lowered its 12-month price target to $61 from $63 as it rolls valuation to Q5-Q8 estimates, which start to include 2028 LOEs (e.g. Eliquis). The target multiple rises to 10.5x Q5-Q8 P/E from 10x to reflect the Pharma sector re-rate. Rating stays Neutral.

GS model changes: FY26 revenue +0.2% to $50.5bn, adjusted EPS +1.5% to $6.55. FY26 Sotyktu revenue raised 18.6%, and Revlimid, Sprycel and Abraxane raised on more durable near-term revenue. FY26/27/28 EPS are $6.55/$6.83/$5.41 vs prior $6.45/$6.83/$5.52.
GS revenue forecasts fall from $50.5bn in 2026 to $49.3bn in 2027 and $41.7bn in 2028, the year of the Eliquis LOE.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $61 from $63 as valuation rolls to Q5-Q8 estimates that include 2028 LOEs, partly offset by a higher 10.5x P/E multiple. GS sees the stock as balancing risk/reward ahead of the clinical readouts.

sector_views.rationale: GS cites a favorable recent rotation into Pharma and a sector re-rate, which lifted its BMY target multiple to 10.5x from 10x.

earnings_insights: BMY 3Q26 results were generally inline per GS, a modest beat and raise per its First Take. Reported 10/29/2026 with growth portfolio products ahead of consensus: Opdivo Qvantig +5%, Breyanzi +8%, Sotyktu +16%, Yervoy +5%, Opdualag +4%. Cobenfy missed consensus by about 16%.
GS FY2026E estimates (new vs prior): revenue $50.5bn vs $50.35bn, adjusted EPS including guided IPR&D $6.55 vs $6.45. FY27E EPS $6.83 unchanged, FY28E EPS $5.41 vs $5.52.
GS quarterly EPS: 2Q26 $2.04 (actual), 3Q26E $1.35, 4Q26E $1.58, 1Q27E $1.58. The 3Q26E figure is shown as a GS estimate in the estimates table even though the quarter has been reported.
FY25 adjusted EPS was $6.15 and revenue $48.2bn. GS forecasts revenue of $50.5bn in 2026, $49.3bn in 2027 and $41.7bn in 2028. The adjusted EPS forecast for 2028 is $5.41.
risk_factors: Milvexian SSP and Afib readouts: a negative outcome, or readacross from Bayer's asundexian, would hurt the DCF. Afib is the biggest swing factor.
Legacy portfolio erosion from LOEs, including Eliquis in 2028, and IRA implementation could exceed GS forecasts.
Slower growth from the growth portfolio (Cobenfy, Camzyos, Reblozyl, Opdualag, Breyanzi).
Cobenfy destocking and volume growth that lags expectations.
Negative pipeline outcomes, e.g. Cobenfy in Alzheimer's disease psychosis or milvexian AF.

tension_points.bull_case: Management points to a solid Phase 2 showing 30% stroke risk reduction, careful dose selection and a randomization window chosen for best efficacy, and says the pipeline is broad and rich.
tension_points.bear_case: Bayer's asundexian set a high bar and its result could read across to the milvexian Afib trial, the greatest swing factor on GS's DCF. Investors are concerned about risk/reward.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A negative milvexian SSP or Afib readout would invalidate the bull case. The SSP readout is expected before year-end.
